utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning, gentlemen. Mr. Wladimiroff, you are standing

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have good news for us early this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I hope so. Before the Prosecution calls its next witness, I want to raise a matter that is related to witnesses to come. That concerns a notice that has been given to us by the Prosecution that the Prosecution will use a photospread for identification purposes to witnesses. This photospread consists of 13 black and white photographs among which is a photograph of Mr. Tadic. After inspecting the material that has been shown to the witnesses, we have been evaluating the sense or nonsense of this test. I want to make some comments on that before we go to the next witness, if the court pleases. The test, your Honours, is not original evidence ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am sorry. To understand it, I think I need to understand better what it is that is proposed by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. To start with, I think I should say that the test is not original evidence. It merely is a demonstration of a theory that a party may have as to a particular issue in the case. Therefore, any tests that are sought to be used to demonstrate a theory must be based upon legitimate procedures to ensure their validity. This has not been achieved by the identification procedures used in this case. So we object to any testimony given by witnesses on the basis of this photospread if the accused was already known to the witness before the alleged crime or if the witness took part in a previous identification test. It is a basic rule of identification procedure that involvement in a crime cannot be proved by means of a line-up or a show-up when the suspect is already known to the witness for other reasons than involvement in a crime. Identification on the basis of a photospread by a witness who already knew the suspect has no probative value at all. This is generally accepted in forensic psychology and in legal practice. If the Prosecution intends to examine a witness on the basis of the photospread which, as I already said, is composed by 13 photographs in black and white, among which is a photo of Dusko Tadic, it will have to demonstrate that the witness did not know the accused before the alleged crime and that the witnesses were not shown photographs of the accused at a previous occasion. We also object to any testimony given by witnesses on the basis of the Prosecution's photospread if it does not provide for an unbiased identification test. It needs no explanation that a photospread should not contain such suggestive details or biasing elements that it can be used to identify the accused even by those who do not know his face. To test this the spread should be shown to a number of persons who are completely naive with respect to the identity of the accused. This test is known as the Doob and Kirshenbaum test. This test has been performed on behalf of the prosecution with a group of Dutch persons. The scientific guessing level, which is the number of persons that can be expected to select a picture of Mr. Tadic, was calculated to be three persons out of this group. The test, however, showed that more persons, in fact five persons, chose the photo of Mr. Tadic. If one likes mathematics, such a difference between the expected and observed guessing level is not statistically significant, but mathematics is not the right criterion here. The value of the Doob and Kirshenbaum test is that any deviation of the calculated guessing level should lead to a rejection of the test. Usually, subjects in a Doob and Kirshenbaum test are selected from the same ethic group as the witness. A specific reason is that membership of ethnic groups may be obvious to those who grew up in the former Yugoslavia. Whereas the Doob and Kirshenbaum test was performed with a group of Dutch persons, this ethnic aspect may not have played a significant role. Nevertheless, more persons than the calculated guessing level chose the photo of Mr. Tadic. If the photospread is composed of photographs of males of different ethnic groups of the former Yugoslavia, the deviation of the calculated guessing level outcome of the test will even be worse if it will be performed with persons from the former Yugoslavia who have not seen pictures of Mr. Tadic before. We have no knowledge of a Doob and Kirshenbaum test being performed with persons from the former Yugoslavia. The validity of an identification on the basis of the photospread is, as far as we know, not properly tested. Whereas "the Dutch test" has shown that the accused has been chosen above the guessing level, we reject the value of any identification on the basis of the Prosecution photospread. The presentation of a photospread also containing photographs of Bosnian Muslims or Croats (or even worse non-Yugoslavs) to non-Serb witnesses further invalidates the choice frequency. In our opinion, a photospread may only have probative value in this case if it only shows photographs of Serbs of an appearance generally similar to the accused. If the Prosecution intends to examine a witness on the basis of the photospread, we take the position that it will have to demonstrate that the spread shown to the witness was composed by photographs of Serbs only. At all events, we should realise that the logic of an identity test is that a recognition of a suspect by a witness should only have one and exclusive explanation, that is, the witness has seen the suspect at the scene of the crime. If it cannot be excluded that there may have been another occasion on which the witness has seen the suspect, a positive identification cannot logically lead to the conclusion that the witness saw the suspect at the scene of the crime. When there has been a possibility that the witness saw a picture of the suspect, but he says he did not see it, or does not remember seeing it, we must assume that his recognition might have been guided by a memory of which he is not aware. It is a fact of common knowledge that requires no proof that pictures of Mr. Tadic have been shown on television and published in newspapers all over the world since February 1994. If a witness is for this reason guided by his memory, a successful identification only means that the witness knows the appearance of Mr. Tadic. In that case, there is no confusion as to whom he is referring in his testimony, but this does not allow the further conclusion that he saw him at the scene of the crime. Summarising, your Honours, it may be said that identification on the basis of the Prosecution's photospread has no probative value if the accused was already known to the witness before the alleged crime or if the witness took part in the previous identification test, or if it does not provide for an unbiased identification test. In our opinion, questioning the witness on the basis of the Prosecutor's photospread will not provide evidence with probative value. It will only serve a prejudicial purpose and provide apparent legitimacy to a flawed procedure. As long as the Prosecution has not satisfied the court of the opposite, we object to any questioning of the witnesses on the basis of the Prosecution's photospread.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have discussed generally this method of identification and the plans of the Prosecutor at various pretrial conferences. The Judges actually have left it to the parties to get together and determine just how they were going to handle this matter. I gather, at least you got together in that you have spoken to each other about how this would be handled, but there appears to be a significant difference as to the admissibility of such evidence. I think now would be a good time to hear from the Prosecutor, if we may, to hear just what your plans are, once again to tell us how you would propose this because, I must admit, there were some questions that we had during our pretrial conferences about how this would be conducted. What do you plan to do, without obviously offering the evidence, but just tell us the procedures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: You might remember that I was not present at those very early pretrial conferences. I did not form part of the Chamber and did not hear what you proposed with this photospread which I have not heard of before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps in dealing with the question that has been raised by your Honours, I would like to indicate that the issue is not immediate in the sense that it is going to happen with the next witness. I think there has been to that extent some misunderstanding, but I will touch on that. The next witness is clearly a recognition witness, but during the investigative process he was shown a book of photographs purely for investigative purposes. I made that book available to the Defence purely for them, for their own purposes, for them to examine it, but I perhaps did not make clear that I would not be asking this witness about that photo book in the course of his evidence in these proceedings, but that is indeed our position. We will not be asking recognition witnesses, witnesses who are clearly recognition witnesses, to give evidence of any photo books, photospreads that were shown to them in the investigative phase. In saying that, we are not admitting anything in respect of the photospread at all in terms of its probative value or admissibility. It is just that it is not our intention to do that. I was not really anticipating submissions on this this morning so I have not prepared anything in particular about it. I will answer some of the issues that were raised by Mr. Wladimiroff, but I might ask my colleague, Mr. Tieger, to pick up on anything that I leave out in the submission because he has been looking after this particular question for us on behalf of our team. Your Honours, we would submit, and we will be suggesting, that our photospread, the one that we have developed, has been developed properly. It is the best that can be achievable in the circumstances, and with pure ID witnesses it is entirely appropriate, it is admissible and, we say, highly probative. There is, however, an area where I would imagine we are likely to be in most dispute.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you because this is a problem we have had in the past, and that is I do not know that I fully understood what you intend to do. I mean, you have to take me through the procedure. "Photospread" to me means a spread of photos. So you are going to do what? You have shown a spread of photos to the witness before and they have X number of photos and then, I gather, the Defence knew what photos were included in this spread. That is what I am lacking. You will just have to begin from the very beginning for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, perhaps the use of the word "photospread" by me is misleading. It is a booklet containing 13 photographs and these photographs have been specifically selected at our request by people who we consider to have expertise in the field. The process is that the book of photographs is presented to the particular witness and the witness then goes through examining each photograph and then either identifies one or not. In most instances, this will be shown purely to people who we classify as identification witnesses. These are people who do not know the accused, but see a person at a particular site or scene doing a particular act; this is shown to those persons and that person will be asked out of court to see whether or not they can select the photograph. It may happen in some instances -- this has already been done now, but in many instances it will not -- in many instances this will happen when the witnesses are brought here to The Hague in order to give their evidence, so it will happen before they come into court. They will then give their evidence in court as to what they selected in the photo book and that will then be tendered as evidence in the proceedings. So it will be an out of court identification but it may happen at that later stage. In some instances that has already been done, as I have said. In most cases, however, the witnesses are recognition witnesses and the grey area, if I might say, is somebody who says, "Yes, I know the accused in the sense that I have seen him on one or two occasions" or whatever, but that is about the limit of the knowledge of the person or the witness. In those cases, it was our intention to show the photospread and to treat them as if they were an identification witness, because the recognition is of such poor value and this may be an area where it will be disputed. It will be on the side where there is so little evidence of recognition that we would say without more that person needs to be shown an ID. We have obtained expert advice on this process and the same expert has been used by both the Prosecution and the Defence. We do not expect necessarily any ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is a first! The same witness, is that Dr. ---

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Wagenaar.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Wagenaar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At this stage we had not anticipated that there would be any difference in the advice that we had received, and we assume that is the same, it is coming to both sides. But, as I say, it is not this witness that is coming next. I merely gave it to the Defence that has prompted them to have this reaction which I can understand, but it is not going to be necessary for the next witness in any event. But perhaps I might ask Mr. Tieger if he would like to add anything to that because, as I say, he is the one who has been dealing directly with Dr. Wagenaar and this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: May I ask about the next witness though? You say with respect to this witness you did show him the photo book?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In some cases -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In some cases it has happened, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This next witness, you did show him?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As an investigative procedure.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But he is a recognition witness and you would, I gather, attempt to lay the appropriate foundation for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: His prior knowledge, how often he saw him, where he saw him, under what circumstances, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It would be your position if he could identify him without ever having seen the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may want to have some questions, I suppose, then of the witness on that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Well ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am trying to deal with what we have right here, and we do need to get to the larger problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What we have tried to do, your Honour, is to trigger the issue, because we experienced the court accepting a dock identification ---

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: -- and we thought we should raise the matter as early as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As we see it, the best way we should deal with it is, perhaps, a trial-within-a-trial, that is, to hear the expert witness on that issue and that might be the expert we both feel is very competent in this matter, Professor Wagenaar.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is possibly a good idea before we get to ------

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When will you use this then, not this next witness but the witness after?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Not the witness after, your Honour, but there is a witness coming up which we would call a purely identification witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry. When do you expect to have need of this photospread ID, identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About nine witnesses away, your Honour, I think, we expect.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is good. We can put off, of course, ruling on it. I realise I cut you off before you fully explained your procedure, but two things: With respect to the next witness, it appears that the photospread has been shown to the witness but the witness, I gather from what Mr. Niemann says, knew the witness before. So you have been objecting to the dock identification and it has been overruled because there has been a proper foundation. With respect to this next witness, I do not know whether you want to handle it as an objection after we hear the testimony on this photospread or whether you want to ---

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I understand ------

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- or whether you want to interrupt, perhaps, before he makes the dock identification and ask the witness questions about this photospread, that is what I am suggesting, before he even does the identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. That is, I think, the best way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then we can rule on it and see how much this photospread -----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. So before there is a dock ID, or you can talk about it and tell us how you want to handle it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. As I understand it, the Prosecution is not going to use the booklet. They are not going to question the witness on that matter; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But you know now that possibly that they will -----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So now we know, we will ask the witness and then, I think, we intervene at the proper moment to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, then we will do that before we even allow the witness to attempt to give a dock identification, we will allow you to just raise this issue and then we can rule on it. You are suggesting that, perhaps, we hear from Dr. Wagenaar before we even hear these witnesses that are nine witnesses away or so -- did you say nine?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What do you think about that, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It was not our intention to call him as part of our case in-chief, and it would be an unusual move for the Defence to call him in a trial unless we can have proceedings somewhat similar to a voir dire maybe the approach.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But if we had a voir dire, we would not hear from a witness. If Dr. Wagenaar is going to be an expert witness for the Defence, of course, he would then be allowed to sit with the Defence during your attempted offer of the photospread and would be here with counsel with the Defence and advise them as to cross-examination. That is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps I will ask Mr. Tieger to deal with that issue? With Dr. Wagenaar I am not sure what the position would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me there is no question that if this issue is to be raised, it will not be effectively dealt with during the course of a witness's testimony. It has nothing to do, as I understand it, with the witness himself, and it will clearly represent a disruption in the proceeding in so far as the presentation of that particular witness's evidence is concerned. So if the court's question is whether or not we need some form of hearing prior to any testimony from a witness whose testimony implicates the use of the photo book for identification purposes, I think the answer is probably, yes, otherwise we will have a witness sitting in the dock while we litigate issues about which he has no particular knowledge or expertise. To clarify, if it helps, the development of this issue I might adds the following: this was a matter raised with the Defence many, many months ago, at which time we enquired whether or not the Defence expected to object to the procedure that the Prosecution proposed. We were told at that time that the presentation, evaluation and acceptance of this photo book by Dr. Wagenaar, about whom we were both aware, would resolve that issue. In so far as the photo book itself is concerned, we have not heard objections from the Defence prior to this day. Dr. Wagenaar, in fact, was presented with a book, conducted a test, and advised that its use was appropriate. That, in so far as the Prosecution is concerned, was the status of the photo book to this day.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you have heard the objection of the Defence for the first time, do you need some time to prepare a full oral response and you may have that time, since we do not need to resolve this issue until nine witnesses, which may be another week, 30 some hours. Do you want some time to respond to it, because I think I understood Mr. Wladimiroff's presentation. Just in the interest of time -- you say that we need a hearing prior and that is an opportunity for an argument from counsel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In terms of need, I think the issues seem clear enough to me. I do not think so, but I know it is being raised by the Defence and it seems to me inappropriate to do so with the witness sitting in the dock.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Judges will talk about it today and advise you tomorrow how we wish to proceed, perhaps even when we will listen to counsel regarding this whole process. At least I think we have a better understanding of what it is you intend to do, and then at that time you can address the objections of Mr. Wladimiroff as well as his suggestion that we hear from Dr. Wagenaar prior to it. It just seems to me that is a matter of law and a matter at some point he will come and testify and we will listen to what he has to say. So, why do we not then just proceed with the next witness and handle that issue which we have? Then we will have an opportunity to talk among ourselves to see how we want to handle it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, just to better understand your objection: in a case of somebody who knows the accused very well, has grown up with him, I do not understand -- I can appreciate that being shown a photograph adds nothing whatever. On the other hand, it does no harm, does it, for somebody who knows the accused intimately be shown a photograph, I do not why they bother to show him a photograph, but if they do and he gives evidence of it, it is of no significance one way or the other as far as identification is concerned;, whereas you rather put it that it vitiates. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I do agree that indeed it does not add anything. It has no probative value at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But it just sets the atmosphere. We rather prefer to avoid that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, gentlemen, for raising that point and giving us some little time to resolve that issue. Mr. Niemann, are you ready to call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I call Ferid Mujcic. FERID MUJCIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, would you please take that oath that is before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In translation]: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you sir, you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, could you tell the Tribunal where you were born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on 20th April in the village of Brdjani near Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately how far is Brdjani from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My house is about one kilometre away from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you attend your primary and secondary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I attended the primary school in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from a period of time when you worked at a sawmill in Germany, have you lived and worked all your life in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, own land in Kozarac which you worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you own a property in Kozarac, a small farming type property that you worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you by nationality Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 28th March 1973 I went to do my military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you do this, where did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Vipava and then to Ljubljana after a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In what republics are those two places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Republic of Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In the beginning of 1992 were you either in the JNA or the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was your role in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, how shall I explain? It is part of the JNA, but the Territorial Defence, we did not have any particular role.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I was asking more what you did, what your connection to the Territorial Defence was in the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a while we kept guard at the mountaineers' hostel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I might come back to that in a moment. Do you know the accused in this case, Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have known him almost all my life, because we lived in the same place. He lived in the centre of the town and I was one kilometre away from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there any particular circumstances from time to time when you would meet Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In passing, sometimes in a pub, sometimes in this mountaineers' hostel. That is how we met, but we did not have any particular ties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the course of your life when you lived in Kozarac, would you see him from time to time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us approximately whether you saw him rarely, just occasionally or did you see him often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, from time to time I saw him -- I mean, we did not socialise -- in passing, in a coffee bar, but as I lived in that place sometimes I met him fairly frequently, sometimes it would be only from time to time. I did not pay much attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you mentioned earlier that he lived in the middle of the town. Are you able to describe in more detail where he lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He lived not far from the school building across the street from a building where teachers or medical people lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what his premises were used for apart from residential purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a cafe bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So far as you are aware, did he and his family live there all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what Dule Tadic did before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I know is that he had this cafe bar and that he was active in karate; what else he did, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know the name of his father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ostoja.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule's wife?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Dule's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember what her first name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not they had any children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know they had children, but how many I would not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether you knew any of the friends or associates of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Emir Karabasic, I mean, from what I could see before, and then of late towards the end, I did not much heed to who he was socialising with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know who his neighbours were in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Salih Perusa. He lived below Dule's house because I visited that man at his house fairly often even on business, and that was Dule's neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know whether or not Dule Tadic had any brothers or sisters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew he had two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew it, Ljubo and Mladen. That is what they called them in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know the family name of his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Her maiden -- as a girl, she lived in Vidovici and her father was Baja. That is what we used to call him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you saw Dule Tadic and knew him in the town of Kozarac prior to the war, was he a man that was clean shaven or did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes he had a beard, sometimes he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dule Tadic was in any way involved in politics in the period leading up to the commencement of the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I could learn from others, when it came to elections that there was voting at his house; about other things, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you believe that Dule Tadic knew you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever speak from time to time when you met prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would say "hello" to each other in passing by, ask after one another's health -- nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know or know of anyone in the Kozarac area or region who looked like Dule Tadic or who could be confused or mistaken for Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall when the war started in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 24th, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say 24th, do you mean 24th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you on that particular day when the attack on Kozarac commenced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not remember where I was exactly that day, but I know I was not at home; that I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When the shelling started, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We reported to -- we were told by the TO to report in case of something and that is what we did, that is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mountaineers' hostel on Debeli Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is this behind the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is above Vidovici up in the hills above the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have a uniform on or did you put on a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had a uniform and I put it on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this an old JNA uniform that you put on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where had you got this uniform from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were issued them by the Local Commune in Kozarac several years before that, I do not know how many. Before the incident happened we were issued them by TO, by the Reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What sort of weapon did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had an M48 rifle of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you get that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When did you get that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got it about one year before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did you report to on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question. What do you mean, what day?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the day of the attack you said you reported at a place beyond Vidovici; I am asking, who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was to report to Vasif Kulasic, but as he was not there I found a couple of other friends who were also to report there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who is Vasa Kulasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vasif Kulasic, not Vasa. He was a Captain, a TO Captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about the other people in the town, so far as you knew? What did they do at the commencement of the -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was major panic and everybody moved towards the woods, women, children, and we also escaped there and they were with us in the woods, some of them fled in an unknown direction running for their lives from shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you assigned any particular task to perform as a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told to protect women, children, elderly, but there was such panic that we ourselves moved aimlessly, afraid, moving around without any particular objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay up in the mountain beyond Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I am not sure about the time. I know I set off to look for my family. I did not know what had happened to them and where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you find your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After some time, how long did that take, I could not tell you, but I did find them finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then we all flocked together in that area, some stayed in the forest, some rallied below Vidovici, some in Vidovici, looking for shelter from the shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay there for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed in there until Wednesday, until the orders came, I do not know from whom, to move towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say Wednesday, is that the Wednesday after the attack start started on 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you happen to recall what date that was, that Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say with certainty which date it was, but I know it was Wednesday and there was a large mass of people there and they were all withdrawing towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: These were women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Women, children, old people, men -- all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the nationality of these people that were in this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were Muslims and a smaller number of Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were any of the people in the group armed with any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, what we did have from the TO, we had discarded them because we had neither orders nor any particular objectives, so whatever we had we threw them away and moved with our families.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about the military uniform that you were dressed in? Did you do anything with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I went to look for my family I changed and I left it in the house. I put on the first thing that I laid my hands on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened after that? What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I returned to look for my family where as the passers-by had told me, they had seen them, that they were in Vidovici, and that this whole column was in Vidovici and that is where I found my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you and your family then join the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column was moving towards Kozarac and we were walking for how long, I cannot tell you. We arrived in Kozarac, to the entrance into Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got there what did you see at the entrance of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was military there on both sides and up there in my village I saw a tank and the houses burning, and when we came to the main street everybody was running in panic. It was mostly small children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This was the main street of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean when we went -- when we came to the main street?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, I am just asking, you said that there was panic and that people were running in panic in the main street. I am asking you whether it was the main street of Kozarac or the main street of your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was panic from the village up until the main street in Kozarac where the column became much tighter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would ask you, if you would, and might the witness be shown, Exhibit D12, the Defence Exhibit? (Defence Exhibit D12 was handed to the witness) Would you just have a look at that map for a moment, just to orientate yourself to it, and can you tell me, do you recognise what it is a map of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a map of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am wondering if you would do something for me? I would like to place this map on the overhead projector screen which is beside you and, with a pointer that is now going to be given to you, could you as best you can trace the route that you took when you came down from Vidovici to Kozarac for me, please, if you could? Take your time and, as best you can, if you can do it. You will need to point to it on the overhead projector for us to all see what you are pointing to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is hard for me to read the maps, but I will try as much as I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You will need to point to it on the projector, not on the television. Point to the actual map here, if you would not mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If you talk in the direction of the microphone, I think it should pick up your voice. Do you see right in the top right-hand corner the word "Vidovi"? As best you can remember, can you tell us how you came down towards Kozarac, the way that column came down towards Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column went down from Vidovici, down towards Brdjani, towards the mosque. We were approaching Mutnik mosque, between the two graveyards, and then the column started walking on the main street.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is approximately where you your pointer is now, is it? Would you hold it still there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here in Mutnik. This is Mutnik. This is where Mutnik mosque is and this is where we came on to the main street, between the two graveyards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps that might be returned to the Registrar? You might resume your seat again. Thank you, Mr. Mujcic. As you moved down the main street of Kozarac, after having left the area of the Mutnik mosque, what happened then, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember. When we came we were walking by the old school and I came closer to the well because I was at the end of the column, and I saw that by the shop the people were standing by the shop, by the kiosk, and when I took a better look I saw who those people were and who was standing behind them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the people were that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who were standing against the wall with their arms towards the shop and with their backs turned towards us, those were Karabasic Ismet, Karabasic Ekrem, Karabasic Sejdo, Foric Redzep and the fifth person for whom I am not sure, I suppose that that would be Fikret Alic whom I knew, but I am not absolutely sure because I did not have a good look of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were all these people that you saw Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know them all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you get a good view of them when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say they had their arms outstretched, can you demonstrate to the court how they had their arms positioned? You might stand up and just show us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The arms were stretched out towards the kiosk, the shop. Their legs were spread and they were leaning against the shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you could resume your seat again? Can you tell us whether they carried any arms that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What does this pertain to?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am asking you whether Ismet and Ekrem Karabasic and Sejdo Karabasic and those men that we are just talking about, did they appear to have any arms on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they dressed in military clothes or civilian clothes that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from those men that you saw lined up with their arms against the kiosk, did you see anybody else in the area at that time that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Dusko Tadic, I saw Goran Borovnica and Milos Gajic, also known as "Gajo".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you saw Dusko Tadic there, where were you when you first saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was next to the well which is located by a small shoe store at the corner where the road for Kalate leads or where the road for Kalate goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately what time of the day or night this was when you saw Dusko Tadic in this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not recall what time it was because we did not really care about the time. We did not even think about what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether it was day time or night time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was day time, afternoon, but I could not tell you what hour. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you recognise Dule Tadic when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall whether or not he was clean shaven or whether he had a beard at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, he had a very short beard, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately, how far away from him would you have been in metres when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I first saw him it was not very far, because the column was walking and we were approaching.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your view of Dule Tadic obstructed by any thing or person when you looked at him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I first saw him, no, it was not obstructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For how long were you able to see Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Long enough to be able to recognise him clearly and be able to see what was happening during those moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else with Dule Tadic at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to Dule there was Gajic, and in front of Dule was Goran Borovnica who was doing something around Ekrem Karabasic, whether he was searching something around him but, in any case, he was standing by him and I observed this and I saw him hit him with a rifle in the back. I did not see exactly where it was, whether it was the head or the shoulders, but it was that area, that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say you saw him hit, you are talking of Goran Borovnica hitting him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Had you ever seen Dule Tadic and Goran Borovnica with each other on any previous occasion prior to this event and prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that they were friendly. I did not see that before the war. Goran Borovnica used to work as a waiter and I did not really pay attention before the war who was friendly with whom, because this was a large tavern, we used to drop by to that place and Goran Borovnica worked there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was Goran Borovnica a Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell me how Tadic was dressed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was dressed in a military camouflage uniform. He had a camouflage hat on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall whether or not he had any weapons on his person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had, as far as I could observe, a pistol on his, on himself. I could not see what calibre, but it was a longer, longer pistol than usual, than normal pistols, and he also had an automatic rifle. I did not see what automatic rifle it was because those were awkward moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now are you able to say what Dule Tadic was doing with respect to the people who were lined up against the wall with their hands above their heads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He stood behind the back of Goran Borovnica. I could not tell you exactly how far away from Goran, perhaps one metre or a metre and a half, and he stood; when I saw him he was just standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we were walking we came to about halfway of the road and about halfway of the road towards Kalate and this is where the column stopped. At that time I saw that they were transferring people, that they were taking people across the road and that Dule has moved away from there, and because I was in the middle of the column, as I was carrying my little daughter, she was very young and I was carrying her in my arms, and I was worried about myself. So this is why I tried to get to the middle of the column and in that way protect myself from being recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do anything else at this stage to prevent yourself from being recognised, apart from carrying your daughter and move ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was pulling on a coat upwards in order to protect myself and I was carrying my little daughter in my arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you partially obstruct the view of your face with the collar of your coat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I partially protected my face in this way. I am not sure exactly how, to what extent I was able to protect myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you also lift your daughter on to your shoulder and did that also partially obstruct the view of your face, an attempt to partially obstruct the view of your face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now when you did this, did this in turn also obstruct your view of what was then happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Partially, yes, but I still managed to see that in front of the column on the left side Sejdo Karabasic went to the left side of the column, Redzep Foric, as far as I could see, and this person, this person that I think was Fikret Alic, but I am not certain that this was Fikret Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you yourself see Ismet and Ekrem Karabasic go across the front of the column to the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could clearly see only Sejdo and Redzep and this other person, that they crossed to the other side because at that time we were ordered to walk faster. The soldiers ordered this and they were standing on one side, on both sides of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would like you to look, please, if you would at this plan. Might a copy be given to Mr. Wladimiroff as well. I have already given him a copy. There is a copy for the Judges. Perhaps that could be marked 223. Mr. Mujcic, would you please just examine that for a moment and after you have examined it tell me whether or not you recognise what it purports to represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the main street going through Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is this the place where you say you saw those men lined up against the wall; the area of where you saw those men lined up against the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 223 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps the exhibit could be placed on the overhead projector. Mr. Mujcic, I am going to ask you again, if you would for me, to look at this plan on the screen and taking this pen that I give to you I would ask you to make some markings on the plan for me. I think perhaps the best way to do it would be for you when I ask you to hop up and just make the marking and then sit down again so we can pick up your voice on the microphone. First of all, do you see the area on the plan referred to as the Mutnik Mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is at the top of the plan and down the bottom of the plan do you see the word "Trnopolje"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: To the right of the plan the word "Kula"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And to the left of the plan "Kalate"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that the representation of the intersection that you just gave evidence about, and was the column in effect moving from the top of the plan towards the bottom of the plan; in other words, was the column moving from the Mutnik Mosque area down towards Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is this a representation of the main street of Kozarac, the Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are there two roads then leading off, one going to the little village of Kalate, and the other road heading towards Kula which is a town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now taking the pen that I have given to you, would you draw an arrow showing the direction that the column was marching down that street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I get up?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could you make a mark at the place where you say you saw these five men lined up with their hands against the wall, that is, Ismet and Ekrem, Sejdo Karabasic and Redzep, could you make a mark on that plan where you say you saw those men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you just draw an X there at that spot, an X at that spot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you mark on the plan, as best you can recollect, the place where you saw the well in front of the old school was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you put ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is that? Is that a W?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will ask him to do that, your Honour. Would you put a W there at that spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you mark on that plan with the letter T approximately the area where you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you also mark on that plan approximately, write with the letter B, approximately the spot where you saw Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you also draw an arrow in the direction of where you saw Sejdo and Redzep taken across the front of the column, in what direction were they taken would you please draw an arrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. How should I mark this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just draw an arrow and could you put an S in front of it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He wants to know how do you want the arrow to be drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I want you to draw the arrow in the direction that these men were taken. That is a very small arrow. Do you think you could draw just a slightly bigger one for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In front of the other arrow which was the direction the column was going, the bottom arrow going towards Trnopolje, would you put the letter C, the way the column was going. That is it, yes. If you would just put the letter C there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Above or below the arrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Above is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness marked on the plan).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Might that plan be returned to the Registrar. This place where you first saw the five men standing with their hands against the wall, Ismet and Ekrem, Sejdo Karabasic, Redzep Foric and the other gentleman you are not sure of, can you describe what this building was used for? What was the building before the war used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a kiosk, a stand that was used for selling chicken in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you have mentioned a couple of times in your evidence the reference to Kula. What is a Kula in your language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is an old, old building that has remained here in Kozarac from the old times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is a tower is it, an old tower?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there any other major buildings in that immediate vicinity that you can recollect being there prior to the war when you lived in Kozarac, perhaps on the other side of the road from the chicken kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean across the road on the other side?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a supermarket and a store selling cevapi (which is grill) and also the photographers stand, a shop, and a shop which was renting video cassettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I now had proposed showing the video Exhibit 195, but it might be a convenient time perhaps to show that after the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Those other shops were across the street from the chicken building, I gather?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I might get the witness to mark them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is OK. That is what I thought he said, across. Very good. We will stand in recess then until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have made notes of what I told you this morning and, if you would like to have it, I may tender it together with the Rules as drawn by Professor Wagenaar attached to it. If the Prosecution has no objection I will provide you also with a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I assume it is part of Mr. Wladimiroff's submissions and, if that is the case, certainly we have no objection. We would appreciate a copy.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Yes, we accept it. We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The representative from the Registry has reminded me that Exhibit 223 was admitted as a nice clean drawing and then, of course, the witness made marks on it. The Defence has no objection, do you, to the marks?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So I suppose you will have to -- he made marks on the original, did he not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Original, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, then it will be admitted as marked by the witness. Mr. Niemann, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Might the witness be recalled? Your Honour, at this stage I will be asking to show a video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Niemann, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sometimes we forget that we need witnesses and other participants! MUJCIC FERID, continued. Examined by MR. NIEMANN, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, I would now ask that you watch a video and the video monitor, I hope, is turned on so that can you see it, but if you are looking at the screen, might Exhibit 195 be played? Mr. Mujcic, this video will play through quickly. If you see something as we are going through the video, would you ask us to stop and then tell us what it is that you see? The video depicts going up the street in Kozarac and then down again. As we are going up the street, we will do so quickly. If you see anything, tell us and we will stop the video. We will put it on fast forward. As we reach the Mutnik mosque, we will turn around. The video, in fact, turns around and goes down the street. At that stage we will go at normal spread. As we are going down the street, I will get you to explain various features of the street as we go down, so can we play that video now and could it be played on fast forward unless and until we ask for it to be stopped or slowed down? That is Exhibit 195, your Honour. Can you see that on your screen, Mr. Mujcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be played at fast forward? Slow down, a little bit more forward. Perhaps it could be played at that speed. (The video was played) Do you see anything that you recognise that you want to -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Stop now. Could it stop at this point? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we go a little bit backward to the post office, I recognise the post office building and the cinema.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. Could we just scroll back a little bit, please, and could you tell us when to stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. This was the post office in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now go through forward again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The cinema.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just slow down here, please. Play at ordinary speed there. Now perhaps fast forward it up until the mosque. Play on. Now at this stage the camera is being turned around and we are heading back down the street and could it be played at ordinary speed from here on? Can you describe, is this the route that the column was marching on that Wednesday that you came down from Mount Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Stop there. Do you recognise that feature slightly to the left of the centre of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the well next to the old school. We already passed the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could we go back a bit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We will go back a little bit. Can we scroll back a little bit? That big building -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the old school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Very slowly, if we just go forward? Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the right there is first the well, and then the shop of Ramo Hankic. He was the shoemaker. Here he repaired shoes and also made them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is the reddy coloured shop to the right of centre of the screen, is it, as you look at the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is there anything else that you can see on that screen that you wish to point to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really see everything. It has changed. It has been destroyed, but if you could move slightly forward, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Move slightly forward, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the road leading to Kalate, to the right and across the street. The door belonged to the storage space of a discotheque that we had in Kozarac. It was the discotheque, the door in front and a little bit to the left, you have gone -- to the right is to Kalate, to the left were two stands -- because this is not very clear and it is difficult to tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Is that -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A little bit forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just stop there, if we may? Do you recognise that building that we see now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is really very dim. I cannot really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So can we go forward, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment. Stop. There were two stands here, two kiosks were here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "stands" do you mean kiosks? When you are referring to "stands", are you talking about kiosks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kiosks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you scroll back, please? Stop. Is that the stand or kiosk that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is so unclear, that picture is so unclear, I cannot see properly. I do not understand this. This kiosk stand that I see, I do not understand because if this is a road to Kalate, there were no kiosks on the way to Kalate. It was aligned with the main road, but I really cannot see clearly at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The stand or kiosk, I simply cannot figure it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. Can we go forward, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Stop here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two kiosks by the main road, the first one selling chickens and another one was selling bread and other food stuffs, other bakery products, and there was a third one which was a tobacconist stand now behind it. One went to the right behind the lower kiosk to the discotheque and on the corner was the local commune or local office, as we called it, but now these kiosks are gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was it against the first kiosk that you saw those men lined up with their hands against the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, up in the front here, one passed here. There is a tree standing and then a couple of metres further on along the street where one can see something blue, like snow seems to be covering here. One does not see clearly, but that is where the kiosks were, so along the main street rather than to the right where the road to Kalate leads.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. That can be turned off now. After you passed that well that you mentioned in front of the school where you say you first saw Tadic as you were walking in that column, did you see Tadic again as you got closer to that kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came to the centre, midway on the road to Kalate, perhaps not exactly midway, but more or less halfway to Kalate, I could see him very clearly as a person in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you sure that it was Tadic that you saw on this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sure, completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then after you walked past this kiosk? Where did you go to then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I went towards the Banja Luka/Prijedor road. The column was moving in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did the column finally end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It ended up in Kozarusa by a restaurant, by a tavern, we called "Zikina". That is where the separation of men from women and children began.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men were separated, singled out, on a lawn by the tavern, and with the women, children and old people, I do not know what happened and where they went because they went on. They left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go? Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there for a while with many people, and then we were all loaded on to buses and taken to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say you stayed there, you stayed at Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you how long because every minute seemed very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get into Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you how long the journey lasted because to us it seemed very long. From that place to Keraterm, the distance is very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You arrived at Keraterm in the dark, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could still, there were still some daylight when we arrived. It was late, but there was still some daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at Keraterm, what happened to you then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken off the buses there. We were kept between two buses and we waited. We waited for a long time, how many hours, I do not know, I cannot remember; and then we were again pushed on to buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "we", was that men, women and children or just men and if it were men, what was the varying age groups of these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were men only.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately, what was the range of ages of these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it varied. As to the age, I cannot really be very specific. There were people of all age groups in that group where I was. There were young men of 15, 16 years of age, and there were people over 50 whom I knew and who also came with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you taken when you were loaded back on to the buses again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were loaded back on to the buses. We did not know where we were going, but we ended up at Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the course of the journey to Keraterm and then out to Omarska were you beaten or otherwise mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were all sorts of things. I was somewhere in the middle of the bus and I could not see things that were going on in the front, but one could hear filthy language, undignified language.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at Omarska what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived in Omarska we were brought to a building at Omarska and there the first ones to be separated were Esad Karabasic and one Huka Jakovic who used to work in our mountaineering lodge on Debeli Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about yourself, what did they do with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were pushed through the entrance of that building so we went upstairs to the first room, up the stairs to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this big room a large garage, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was a room to the right and the first one was empty and beyond it one had to pass through it, there were walls on two sides, and further on I could see some tubs and something which looked like a toilet, but I did not go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did someone try to escape when you first arrived at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before we entered the building, Huse Tadic tried to escape from the second bus that was coming behind us. We heard shots and later on we heard that he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you taken for interrogation when you were in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Above the kitchen where we had our lunch, usually. It was one floor higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know who you were interrogated by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first person I recognised was Nada Balaban. There was one from Kosovo, he worked at Mrakovica. I do not know his name. I think his surname might be Kos, but I am not quite sure. He is a person of somewhat advanced age, over 50, tall, very skinny and there were some other soldiers.
