utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you interrogated on three occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they asking you questions about your involvement of the TO during the course of your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the interrogations were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you beaten on the first occasion that you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who beat you, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who were those people, but they were in military clothes. There was somebody called Krkan. I did not know him before but I met him on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With what were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they beat with different objects such as batons, feet, boots, open palm, whatever they laid their hands on, those who were in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you rendered unconscious during the course of these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice. I fainted twice during the interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened to you after you lost consciousness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, but when I regained consciousness I was returned to the room -- I mean the first time I fainted I was returned to the room in which I had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was the room located that you were returned to in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the first interrogation they did not take me back to the room where I had been on the floor upstairs. I was taken to a room on the ground floor, and to the left when one would enter, there were dump trucks and from the entrance they would turn to the right and took me to a room where I found other people too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this a very large building where they used to store and repair the big mining trucks that operated the Omarska mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from the times when you were interrogated, were you beaten on other occasions when you were in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall being beaten on 18th June 1992 by Kopka (sic)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Kopka, Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry, that is my pronunciation. Can you tell us about that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that day Kvocka battered me. I was really battered. I returned. He told me to sit next to the door as before and I returned. After that Emir Karabasic was called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you by this stage back in the place where you normally stayed in the camp, this was after the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not where I was when I first came. That was on the upper floor and this was on the ground floor where trucks were, and ---

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- channels where one repairs vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I meant this place where you had been taken to. What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, I had to sit next to the door as I was told. It was 18th June when they were taken out, after a long time. I do not know how -- the time that he left, I do not know, but then Emir Karabasic was taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly but it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know who it is that took out Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guard opened the door and called out his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When the door was open did you look out of the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you looked out of the door what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I looked through the door and I saw Dusko Tadic standing behind the guard and with him another one, slightly taller. They were standing about a metre and a half to two behind the guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was Dusko Tadic dressed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a camouflage army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you notice whether he was armed or carried any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I could see, he had on his belt a pistol and he held a rifle in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the next thing to happen that you can recollect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that shortly afterwards the door opened again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasko Hrnic was called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then did you hear anything happen after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a certain time there was a silence around us in the room where there were many detainees. There was such a silence that one could not hear anything. There was no noise at all. Then we heard the screaming.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from the screaming, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard very bad language.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Although it may be embarrassing for you, can you as best as you recollect tell us the words that you heard spoken out there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is very embarrassing to use this language but I remember those words that were addressed to us, although we did not know who these words were addressed to and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just tell us what you heard, the words that you heard as best you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I have to, and this is very embarrassing, but if I have to, I will try ---

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You should.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- to say those words.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is important that we hear what you said, so although you may be reluctant to repeat the words, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were curses, there were questions as to if I have to fuck a person, then I did not hear what person, and after that there were words that to lick somebody's arse, to smoke the genital organ, to give a blow job to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you hear any other words spoken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that there were very loud screams and they were saying, "Pull, pull stronger", and even now I can hear these words sounding in my ears.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are there any other words that you heard? As best you can, tell us the exact words that you heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am using the exact words that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are there any other words that you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Pull tighter", "squeeze it tighter". These are the words that I heard. The screams reflected great pain. They were deathly moans, but I did not know what has happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then, after you heard these screams?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how long this lasted, but to me it looked very long, because we were in fear and I was in fear myself. After that we heard them calling out the names, the guards were calling out the names, they called Eno Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, after a certain time, one could also hear noise, screams reflecting strong pain, moans, and after that everything went silent because I was afraid, and so was everybody else in the room, we were afraid that they would come and get somebody else because you never knew whose turn it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: From that time to now did you ever see Emir Karabasic, Jasmin Hrnic or Eno Alic again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, after that I personally never saw any of those persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go out the next morning, out into the open area of this large garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to the toilet in the morning, the next morning, where I saw blood all over the walls. I saw broken lumber and I saw pieces of clothes, one shoe that belonged to Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever see the accused Dule Tadic in Omarska camp on any other occasion apart from the one that you have just attested to, testified to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw this person once again when I was in a line to go to lunch, and I was heading from the kitchen towards the white house at the entrance where we were located, in the room where we lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he on his own or was he accompanied by anyone when you saw him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two men in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How were they dressed? How was Dule Tadic dressed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see whether or not he had any weapons with him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he always had weapons on him, but I am not sure as to what kind because one could see on his hip a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long were you then kept in the Omarska camp, for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you how long I stayed in Omarska, and then afterwards we were transferred to Manjaca. I only found out later that there were 170 people left at Omarska behind us when we were transferred to Manjaca and I could not give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you lose weight when were you in the camp at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came to England for medical treatment on September 15th I weighed 34 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How much had you weighed approximately before you went into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My normal, my usual weight has always been 73 to 75 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was your physical condition when you came out of Omarska camp? Had you suffered any injury?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My medical condition was fairly poor because those were the last moments of my life. I was totally beaten up. I was broken, sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you still to this day suffer from some of the effects of the injuries that you suffered in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you interviewed by Tribunal investigators at your home on 6th May this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were notes of the interview taken down during the course of your interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: However, was a statement ever presented to you for signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was the statement ever read to you in total by the interpreter that was present there on that occasion that you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He started reading something, but did not read everything in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you look around the courtroom, please, and do you see the person that you know as Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have discussed this matter earlier today and it might be appropriate as well if my learned friend mentioned whether any photographs have been shown to this witness prior to this procedure taking place. I know the court has ruled already on the procedure and that is not something that we are taking issue with, but there was mention today of the photographic procedure and whether it should be adduced in evidence to put any identification in court in context.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think so. I just do not know that it is appropriate for the Chamber to direct Mr. Niemann to ask the questions. Excuse me, just one minute.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, it appears at least, as we have indicated in earlier rulings regarding identification by a witness of Mr. Tadic in the courtroom, that if the proper foundation is laid, that is, that he had sufficient knowledge as we have indicated, I do not think it is necessary for me to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Now, however, you have raised an additional point. Mr. Wladimiroff raised a point this morning regarding the photospread. My only suggestion was that if you took the position that the photospread somehow would change the court's position that it has expressed previously, then that should come out at some point before the identification is made of Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I would not want to tell Mr. Niemann to elicit those questions because that is not his responsibility. So I do not know how it would be handled. As I have said several times, we are in a Tribunal and it is a new and a different procedure and it is a wonderful creation that we have created. In my system, however, you would ask to take the witness on voir dire and ask them the questions yourself. I do not know how you want to handle it. To be very honest, from what we have heard from this witness thus far, the Judges are inclined to overrule the objection in any case because, consist with our prior rulings, Mr. Niemann has elicited from this witness a sufficient foundation, but you may know something that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will leave it with Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Then are you finished? At this point I interrupted the witness. You had asked him if he could identify Mr. Tadic. You should repeat the question, if you will. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Mr. Mujcic, would you please look around the courtroom and tell me whether or not you see the accused Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you point to him and describe where he is in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is sitting between two policemen and he is dressed in a greenish suit. He has a tie and he is looking directly at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the record reflect that, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. The record will so reflect that the witness has identified Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions of this witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, I want to ask you some questions about the events that took place when you returned to Kozarac village or town after the shelling of the town had stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was advising you what I was going to ask you questions about. You have told us that that was a Wednesday and that with many other people you returned to Kozarac in a convoy which had originated from Vidovici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the people in that convoy just those who had been sheltering in Vidovici or did it also include people who were joining the convoy who had been sheltering in the woods around Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everything was -- people were moving from Vidovici and other side roads, from Nagrijenac, because there were a lot of people, a lot of men, a lot of children, children, and everything was moving heading towards Kozarac, down along Brdjani road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right, is it not, that the shelling of the town had stopped by then and there was a move of the population down from the hillsides into the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody who was in that area in Vidovici and on the right side from the Modrinac direction, everybody was moving towards Kozarac down from Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have told the court that you were at or towards the end of this convoy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that I was towards the end or towards the middle because I did not know where the end or where the middle or where the beginning were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us at all what position you were in in the convoy? Were there many people left in Vidovici when you left it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how many remained where, but the column was, there was a column -- there were people behind me and there were people in front of me in the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The numbers of people involved in this convoy, was it a great many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A great many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As the convoy progressed into Kozarac, did many more people join it from the surrounding roads and buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give you an answer to that because I was not paying attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get from Vidovici down to the Mutnik mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how long it took us because nobody even thought of measuring the time it took. We were fighting for our own lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what time the convoy started moving from Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afternoon, and I do not know exactly what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you set off on this convoy, did you know where you were going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware, then, that Serb soldiers had taken control of Kozarac town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had heard from others, but I was not sure myself until I saw it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You changed out of your JNA uniform because you would have expected to be at great risk to have continued to wear such clothing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You changed out of your JNA uniform because you were aware that if you had worn it you would have been in great risk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there others who had also changed out of their military clothing into civilian clothes that you were aware of in that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see anybody else, because where I changed in my house there was no-one else changing their clothes with me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were in that column moving from Vidovici down to Kozarac, would it be right to say that the people in that column were very frightened and fearful of what might happen to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we started from Vidovici towards Kozarac everyone was frightened and in panic; people did not know what was going to happen to them and this is how I felt myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you help me at all again as to how long it took you to get from Vidovici down to the Mutnik mosque area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give you the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What it just a long column of people? You could not see the head of the column and you could not see the back of the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you arrived into Kozarac town itself, in the area of the Mutnik mosque, what was the situation in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The soldiers stood on both sides, everybody was frightened, that is normal. The houses were burning on each side. We were directed and we came to the main road and then they made us march down the main street of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say the main road you mean Marsala Tita Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that street goes through Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you join that street in the area of the Mutnik mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came down from Brdjani. We came to Mutnik mosque and this is where, when we came to the main street, we turned to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The soldiers that you saw in this part of the town, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see any other military vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were tanks, and other vehicles. In the locations where they were standing, I could not tell you exactly what locations. I know that I saw one in Brdjani, a tank, and I am sure about it. I am sure about where it stood and others were in different locations and we did not pay attention to what stood where.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were fires; would it be right to say that there were a large number of buildings on fire on both sides of Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, that added to the confusion and fear that all of you had in that convoy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it did. There was a lot of excitement because people were moving down and it took a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the column fill the width of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the whole street, somewhere it did, somewhere it did not, and this is how the column moved. It depends on how they allowed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there any motorized vehicles in that column that you were part of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were tractors, carts with horses, as far as I could see, and I do not know about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you on foot or travelling in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have mentioned being with your daughter. Would it be right to say that you were in a group that consisted of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember any other names of people who were with you at that time in that convoy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because everybody just looked for a place for himself and moved there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was not thinking of members of your family, but any other friends that you may have had in that column at that time that you were moving through Kozarac who were with you whom you could name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything more except there was my wife and my children because there were people moving forward and then lagging behind. I could not really name anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There came a stage when you came to this junction where the road turns right to Kalate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were at that stage on Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect how long you had been walking in Marsala Tita Street for when you came to that junction of the road to Kalate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is not very far from the road which we took to reach the main road. The distance is not particularly big there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did it not take you very long before you had reached the Kalate junction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did it take you only a short while before you reached the Kalate junction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how long it took me. I cannot remember. All I am saying is that the distance is quite short between -- from the place where one takes the main road to this junction to Kalate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you been walking for a long while in that convoy before you reached that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the very beginning, from Vidovici, I was with that column all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had had four days since the attack on Kozarac took place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Wednesday when we set off to Kozarac, how many days had passed, I paid no attention to that and I cannot really say, but I do know that it was Wednesday when we set off from Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have been told and it is a matter of record that the attack on Kozarac took place on the Sunday in the early afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what time of the day it was when there was the attack on Kozarac, but the date was the 24th. That is when the shelling of Kozarac started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In those four days, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, you had been surviving in very difficult circumstances; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There had been shelling of your home town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had seen the destruction of property?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not see the destruction going on, but later on when I passed through it, I saw it here and there smoke going up while we were in Vidovici, and I could not see how the destruction was taking place because one was trying to save one's life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had seen the fleeing of people from their home town out into the woods and hills nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you been able to eat much during that time, those four days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It never occurred to me to eat anything or drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you got much sleep during those four days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if I slept then. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have a bed to sleep in during those four days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who would stay in bed yet expecting a shell to fall on him any time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So by the time you reached Kozarac on that Wednesday, would it be right to say that you were very tired and had had probably the most difficult period of your life to live through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You would have been hungry, thirsty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I experienced no hunger and no thirst at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, you were very tired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not feel even any fatigue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you think that is something you were denying to yourself that you felt fatigue or do you think that, in fact, you were an exhausted individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no time to think about such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, the others around you were in the same condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you get to the area of Marsala Tita Street, was that the first time in that area that you had seen Serb troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that area? I do not know what question you are asking me there. I do not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you seen any Serb soldiers before you reached Marsala Tita Street in Kozarac on that Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were also downhill from Brdjani on the left and right-hand side, there were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you have passed through Brdjani on your way from Vidovici to Kozarac on that Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there many Serbian troops in Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From both sides there were soldiers, I do not know how many. I could not give you the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The column that you are in moving down Marsala Tita Street is also moving through Serb soldiers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The column that you are in moving down Marsala Tita Street is also moving through Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column in which I was and which was moving down Kozarac on the left side, on the right side, were Serb soldiers and those who were moving were civilians, not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The soldiers you have told us were directing which way the column should go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we reached the high street the column turned to the left. I do not know who directed it there but, at any rate, they headed in that direction and that is where I saw Serb soldiers on the right side, and probably they were showing to go to the left and not to the right where they were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we look now at the plan you produced to the court this morning -- Exhibit 223, your Honours -- and if a copy could be placed before the witness and put on the overhead projector? As I understand it, Mr. Mujcic, this is a drawing that was made by you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I look at it there because here I cannot see it very well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Is this a drawing by you, Mr. Mujcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I only made those signs, the arrows, but the plan was drawn by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As I understand it now, someone else from the Prosecution had drawn the layout for you in advance; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. All I did was show the arrows, the directions and I put the arrows down there, and when I was asked various things I marked them, and that is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to look carefully at the "X" where you have placed the men on this plan. That is a spot that you would have walked past, you say, when the column was moving through Kozarac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many men did you see with their arms up against the shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you seen any of those five men earlier in the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember seeing them. I do not recall even some days before that or that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were moving down Marsala Tita Street, is it your evidence that you first saw those men when you were at the position of the well near the old school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day as we were moving down the road I saw them for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had not seen them arrive in that position or being taken to that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, all I saw was Goran doing something around Ekrem Karabasic and I saw him hit him with a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On this plan that you have made your markings upon, if you look carefully at the position you have put Mr. Tadic and Borovnica ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- they would be standing between the men and the shop; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How could it be between those men and the shop when men are leaning against the shop and Goran and another, Gajic, was standing behind, only Borovnica was next to those men. It could not be between the shop but behind their backs towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking you because this is your drawing -- this is not my drawing, you understand -- and you have marked the letters "T" and "B" on the side of the place where the men have been indicated by an "X" in a place where the kiosk would have been; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The men were standing next to the kiosk with their arms up where there is the "X" mark, and Dusko and Gajic were standing behind them, roughly at this distance I have indicated, and Borovnica was next to them and behind them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From your evidence this morning, I understood you to say -- correct me if I am wrong -- that the men had their arms outstretched and were leaning against the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was no building, it was a kiosk, and with their arms up. They had their arms against the kiosk, against the wall of the kiosk, and with their legs spread.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The kiosk faced on to Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, length-wise and it was -- and the window opening was overlooking the Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You showed us on the video film the space that now exists on the high street of Marsala Tita Street where the kiosks are no longer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think you told us that there were two kiosks; one kiosk that sold tobacco and another kiosk that sold something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first kiosk where Karabasic and others were was selling chickens and the other one various bakery products, a third was a tobacconist's, and they had only one wall, one wall was for the kiosk selling tobacco and cigarettes and the one selling bakery products, whereas the kiosk selling chickens was some half a metre away from these other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So where do you say, according to this plan, first of all, Goran Borovnica would have been standing? Is it where you have indicated or somewhere else on the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where was the kiosk? The kiosk was where it is marked with an "X", and it ran along the road, and they were standing at the front of the kiosk with their arms up and Borovnica was behind them and about a metre behind Borovnica, I would not know exactly, perhaps a little more or a little less, were Dusko and Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So have you put on this plan the words "T" and "B" in the wrong place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How could I put them in the wrong place? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because they appear at the moment, as you look at the plan, to be standing in between the men and any building that those men would have been standing against?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I marked with an "X" the building, not the building but a kiosk, but the kiosk is not so big as this "X", it was wider, so that five men could fit there as I saw them, as I saw them standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. If that is your evidence that you marked with an "X" where the kiosk was, have you put Borovnica and Tadic on the Kalate side of the kiosk rather than on the Marsala Tita Street side of the kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not towards Marsala Tita Street, but in that direction, but not down the Kalate road but, rather, on the corner as we come down and where the corner to Kalate is. It was perhaps two or three metres from the corner, I could not say exactly, is where the kiosk was, and by the kiosk where Karabasic is and Borovnica was standing behind Ekrem, and Dusko was a metre, a metre and a half, further on. Nobody could make that estimate where it is marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Borovnica have his back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw, as he was frisking a criminal, whatever, he was looking for something, I do not know what it was. Yes, he was, then he turned away because he was not standing still in one place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But for a period of time Borovnica had his back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw him, yes, he had his back to me, the first time I looked at him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any other activity towards those men leaning up against the kiosk that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any other activity, other than the searching of Ekrem Alic, by Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he straightened up and struck him with the rifle. I could not see whether he hit him in the head or the shoulder. I could not see that, but I saw him strike at him with his rifle, with his rifle butt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "him", you mean Borovnica struck Alic with his rifle butt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Alic, there was no Alic -- Ekrem Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: My mistake. I am sorry. My mistake. But it was Borovnica who did the hitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that four of the men were taken down the street towards the old tower?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I said that I saw Sejdo Karabasic, Redzep Foric and this one about whose name I am not certain, I saw him crossing to the left in the direction of Kula. They crossed to the left from the kiosk when the column was -- came to a halt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So how many men were taken from that position of the kiosk towards the old tower?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly how many, but I saw these three persons clearly behind the child. As I raised my child to hide my face, I was looking leftward and I saw clearly those three.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Until you saw those men being taken in that direction, had you seen any other activity in relation to the men by the kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question? I was coughing and could not understand all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Until you saw those men being taken towards the old tower, had you seen any other activity that you have not told us about that occurred to those men leaning against the kiosk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what you want me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am just asking you, sir, to tell us, if you can, what you saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see why -- I did not see, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the time that you were moving down Marsala Tita Street, the man you say was Tadic had his back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the time that you were moving down Marsala Tita Street, the man you say was Tadic had his back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, what was he doing then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw him by the well he was standing, he was facing the column and he was looking up and down, I mean, towards the column, so it is quite clear that he was facing towards us and not that he had his back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He was not concerned or doing anything with the men leaning against the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just to make it clear, you see, what I suggest to you is that you did not see Dusko Tadic here on that Wednesday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am really sorry, but I said clearly that Dusko Tadic was standing there on the corner behind Goran Borovnica with Gajic where I saw him. It cannot be that I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Even allowing for this possibility that if you did see someone that you were mistaken that it was Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can -- it will be the same mistake as if I said today that I was not here. If somebody said that I was not here today, it would be the same kind of mistake that I could make with regard to my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you make a mistake then in putting the positions of the people on this plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, that is a convenient moment for the afternoon adjournment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Have you completed cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have not no, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess then for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. In the short adjournment we set up one of the visual aids for this section of the questioning of the witness -- hopefully, it will work.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is the first time I have seen it. MR. KAY (To the witness): Mr. Mujcic, I now want to ask you some questions about Omarska and, in particular, the day of 18th June that you gave evidence about earlier this afternoon. One thing was not clear to me, but were you telling the court that on that same day you were beaten by a man called Kovocka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot hear very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps your volume needs to be adjusted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps the interpreters will say something to you to see if it is coming through?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The second time you spoke he said "yes".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking you questions about 18th June and you told the court that on that day a man called Kvocka beat you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, that I was beaten on that day by Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that a man whose name is spelt K-O-V-O-C-K-A?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kvochka, K-V-O-C-H-K-A.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he the Deputy Commander of Omarska camp at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he an interrogator or was he an ordinary guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a guard and he was dressed in a policeman's uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect what time of the day it was that he beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember what time of the day it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he beat you as part of an interrogation or was it an assault upon you in other circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took me out into the toilet area. I do not know why he beat me, but he did beat me and he did that several times prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On that day were you in a room on the ground floor of the hangar of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question because the sounds are not very clear so I did not understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On that day were you in the ground floor of the large hangar where the dumper trucks were kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a room where I lived which was on the ground floor, and you would get to their room by passing by through the garage where the trucks and other vehicles were repaired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the day that you say that Emir Karabasic was called out of the room, were the hangar doors open or closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door to the room were closed at the time when Emir Karabasic was called out. This is not a hangar; it is a room where we were living at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see before you, Mr. Mujcic, a model of the camp at Omarska. What I would like to do now is for you to have an opportunity to look at that model and indicate to the court which room you were staying in. Perhaps if someone could take the roof off the main building that might help the witness? Thank you very much, Miss Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I get up to see better because I cannot see very well from where I am?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, you may. I do not know you need both of your microphones on. If we have four on, the sound really becomes very low. Did you have both microphones on for a reason, Mr. Niemann? If he needs it, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may stand up, sir, and when you do just make sure you are talking through the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will take it in stages, but there the main building which we call in this court the "hangar" is before you with the roof lifted off. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it in that room that the dumper trucks were placed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see from the inside because I am facing the other side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I had hoped that if we pressed a button that this camera here would be able to show us on our screens the building itself.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The witness said he cannot see from standing over there in any case. So the question is, how do we solve that problem? He can come around this side, I suppose, then he will be without a microphone, but he might be able to follow your question and then return to the witness stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. What I am trying to do is orientate you with this building, Mr. Mujcic. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you looked at -- the screen keeps on changing.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you want him to use a pointer? Do you want him to use a pointer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That might help, your Honour, yes. (To the witness): Can you look at your screen? Can you see there the inside of the hangar, Mr. Mujcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is hard to tell because it .....

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Why do you not invite him to walk around?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He can move. Let us not make it difficult, let us make it easy, OK, if you want an answer? Do you want him to point out where he was; if so, he may remove himself from the seat and come over and point to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was going to be the next stage, your Honour, after I had tried everything else. (To the witness): Sir, if you take your headphones off and if you would like to move round to the well of the court -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger? Just a minute, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Very quickly, your Honour; we are advised by the technical people that at some point, if the court deems necessary or counsel deems necessary, the camera can be adjusted somewhat to zoom in or out. I just wanted to advise the court. I have no suggestions to offer.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sometimes I call Gert Jan Stephen Spielberg, but this is really not a movie production. It is really very simple. We are all very together here in a very small courtroom and it is easy for the witness to move if you want an answer to your question. OK?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Come around, Mr. Mujcic, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, when the witness is around here, he understands a little bit of English, as I understand, but if he is given instructions without his headphones he may not understand what the instructions are.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Ask him the question when he is standing there so he can hear your question. He will move around, point and answer your question and then go back and repeat in English any Serbo-Croatian that he may wish to say. MR. KAY (To the witness): Perhaps if you could put your headphones back on, sir, and I apologise for the inconvenience that is taking place. What I would like you to do is to go round and look at that model and to identify which room you would have been staying in on the day that Karabasic was called out. To do that, you will need to take your headphones off and walk around and look at the model yourself and then come back to your seat. Perhaps Miss Sutherland could take off the other lid as well? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you understand, Mr. Mujcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Very good. Take your headphones off and come around and point to the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can the top floor be taken off as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The entrance is here (Indicated), and here you go to the right. I cannot remember which are the doors to the toilet, but I see a glass door here, which are marked by glass, and somewhere here were the metal doors and this room is marked like this, as indicated here. I was sitting here by the door, by the little door, leaning against the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you give the number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 17 was the number of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is what number, the number of the room -- put your earphones on, Mr. Mujcic -- the number of the room that what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The way it is marked there, this is how the room in which I was looked because it had the long corridor, but the door does not look exactly the way it looked in my room, because those were large metal doors and then after that there was a small door through which we entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that room was there also Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At that time when he was called out he was sitting at the table to the left from the door next to the wall, and closer to the corner in the back side of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The door to that room is a metal door; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before the name was called out the guard opened that door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before saying anything, the door was opened and then the guard called out the name of Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many other people were in that room with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The room was full. It was completely full.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Besides people being in the room, were there any other implements, benches, tools?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the left as soon as the door was open there was a plank that looked like a bench and this is where people sat down. People that were beaten, we would normally let them lie down on that plank; and in this corner to the left is a bit cut in and there was another table, a metal table. The top of the table was metal. I do not remember exactly what colour it was. People sat on that table and sat below that table, under the table; and then further on, closer to the end of the wall, maybe a metre, one metre or a metre and a half from the wall, there was another table on which people also sat and at that time, exactly at that time, Emir Karabasic was on that table and under the table there were other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The light into that room came from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The light came from the window, from the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The windows at the back of the room do not come all the way down to the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They occupy an area at the top of the wall; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what sort of size those windows were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were not large windows, and I could not tell you how high they were, maybe half a metre or a bit less than that, and they were -- in the left corner underneath the window there was a trunk, a small trunk, about this size.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The door that you told us about was set in a big metal panel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were the doors that could be -- that were large and then within those large doors there were smaller doors and maybe they were about one metre wide, the smaller doors, and sometimes they would use the larger doors, sometimes they would use the smaller doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On this day when the guard opened the door, would it be right to say that he opened the small door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That small door opened into the big hangar where the dumper trucks for the mine were stored; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they would open towards the trucks, to the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The doors to the hangar where the trucks drove into the garage were closed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether those doors in front, if you mean these doors that are marked white, I do not remember if they were open or closed but they were mostly closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. The doors I am referring to are the rolling doors that are white on the model.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those doors are mostly closed, those doors in front, the white doors that could be raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You also said that Jasko Hrnic was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he in the same room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember whereabouts in that room he was when he was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With Karabasic -- he was sitting with Karabasic out at the table, on the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that time were there any other people called out from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, not, not from that room in which I was and in which Emir Karabasic and Jasko Hrnic were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When those two men went out you said that you heard bad language and screaming. Was that soon after they had left your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, for a while there was silence. It was such a silence that I cannot even describe it. Then after a certain time we heard that language and then after that we heard moaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was next to the door. I was leaning against the big metal door next to the small door. I was ordered to stand there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had been standing there for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would crouch down or straighten up and stand there, but I had to be there because this is what I had been ordered a few days before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So had you been standing in that position for a very long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean? At that time, the first time when they were called out I was standing, I was -- I was sitting and I had my back against the door. I was not standing at that time. I was sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It may be my fault but it is not clear to me whether you are standing or sitting when the door was opened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time when the guard came in to fetch Emir I was sitting and I was leaning against the large metal doors next to the small doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When Jasko Hrnic was called out, whereabouts were you then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the same spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So that would still be sitting and leaning against the wall; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I also, after Emir came out I crouched down and I remained there because I always was at that spot. I was not allowed to move away from there and I remained at that spot even after Jasko went out next to the door, but I cannot remember if I was crouching when Jasko came out or whether I was sitting at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember whether the small door opened into the room where you were or into the hangar area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The small doors opens outward towards the hangar, not into the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say you were leaning against the wall when you were sitting down -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not against the wall, not against the wall, but the big metal door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the metal door against your back or against your side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The metal door could not be to the side of me if I was leaning against the big metal door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As the door opened out, whereabouts in relation to the door as it opened were you sitting or crouching?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time the door opened I was sitting, I think, and the next time I was either sitting or crouching, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So as that door opened out into the hangar, were you on the hinges side of the door or where the door handle and the lock would have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the door opened outward. It opened towards the lower part of the hangar, rather than towards the toilet. I remember that. I remember I was sitting where the handle is, where the door opens. I am not positive about that, but I think I remember that. A long time has elapsed since and one has lost so much since and forgotten, and I do not want to remember those terrible events I went through there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it frightening for you every time a guard opened the door to that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was frightening, very.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were sitting down or crouching and on this occasion you would have been looking up to the guard who had opened the door; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is when the door opens, you turn and look at who is at the door and why it is being opened. I cannot look straight toward the door if I am leaning with my back against the big metal door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right, you looked at the man who opened the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guard's?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Him you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, the name of the guard who opened the door.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is that you did not see Dusko Tadic standing behind that guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot say that I did not see him when I did see him and I guarantee this with my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After Omarska you went to Manjaca, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the end in Omarska camp I went to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you discuss with other people what they said had taken place in the Omarska camp to Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whom you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just with others generally, did you discuss what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they always talked about difficulties, about sufferings. I was not alone there or Emir Karabasic and I only. There were thousands of people who were in prison there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have said that Dusko Tadic was there behind the guard when the door was opened because others have told you that he was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, you cannot say that I heard it from others when I saw it with my own eyes and suffered so much in that room, tortures and beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you were sitting down or crouching down looking up at a guard who opened the door. The room behind you cannot say had the doors open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are asking me unreasonable questions, because I said it and I stand by it where I was leaning against the metal door and that the door opened towards the garage, and when the door opened I looked over my shoulder, through the door at what was going on and it was not different, because I was by the door and nothing else could have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you hear Eno Alic's name being called out by the guards later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Jasmin Hrnic went out it took a long time, I do not know how long it seemed to me, it was long. I heard the guard, whoever it was, call out Eno Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Eno Alic was not in your room, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true that Eno Alic was not with me in my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the guard call out the name of Eno Alic into your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guard never opened the door in my room, nor said anything about my room. We only heard a voice calling out to Eno Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was something that you heard rather than someone telling you that Eno Alic had been called out as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody told me anything. I heard it and many others who were in that same room with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, you have said that you saw Dusko Tadic in Omarska camp on another occasion, do you recollect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recollect seeing him one day when we were going to have lunch. He was coming from the direction of the kitchen towards a part of the house and the entrance, where the entrance and exit door was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that before or after the incident on 18th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was after that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can help me as to how you know it was 18th June that an incident concerning Emir Karabasic happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was severely beaten up on that day and I remember it only too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I am interested in is how you knew with such certainty that it was the date of 18th June? Did you have a calendar with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not have a calendar, but I am positive 18th June was that day because for the past two or three days they had beaten me terribly, and so it is carved in my memory. I shall never forget 18th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you remember me asking you questions earlier this afternoon about the dates of the attack on Kozarac, and you told me that you could not give any date; all you knew was that it took place place on a Sunday and when you went into Kozarac it was a Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were returning -- as a matter of fact, as we were going towards Kozarac from Vidovici I know it was a Wednesday. I do not remember the date. I gave nothing -- I did not identify any day except that Wednesday when we were coming down to Kozarac from Vidovici. As far as I can remember, I never mentioned any Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: All I am interested in is how you give this date of 18th June. Did you have a calendar with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a calendar with me, but whilst I was in the camp I enquired about that day because that Kvocka had really beaten me that day. I still feel pain in my back which is permanently damaged. My head was broken many times, not once. My leg was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can help me, if you can, who gave you then the date of 18th June and told you, "Today is 18th June"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember who told me, but many people said, yes, it was 18th and who was it. They were all friends who were in prison together with me in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or did anyone a long while after Emir Karabasic was called out of room 17 tell you what happened and told you the date of 18th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody had to tell me what happened. The news spread immediately the next day what had happened to Emir Karabasic when we went to the toilet, and it was not Emir Karabasic which related to that date. I remember the date that was related to me personally and I remembered it only too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right, the news spread and there was a lot of talk about it amongst the people in the camp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The news spread if anything was learnt but what you hear with your own ears and see with your own eyes, then it is only natural that you do not need anyone to tell you something or anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because what I suggest to you is that you did not see Dusko Tadic at Omarska on that day or the other day that you have told this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of what do you tell me that I had not seen him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am putting the assertion to you, as I am required to do, for you to accept or deny.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that I had not seen Dusko Tadic the first time in the door or the second time on the pista. I said that I had seen him and I give you my word. With my guarantee with my life in 10 years, in 15 years time I shall give you the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know Miso Damicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean Miso Danicin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miso Daanicic, no, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, do you have redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Mujcic, you were just asked some questions about knowing about 18th June 1992. Do you recall an event on 16th June 1992 when some biscuits were shared by Hrnic with you and other inmates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there something about this incident that informed you of the date at that particular time? If so, can you tell us what it was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I just raise an objection here, your Honour, because my learned friend, as I see it, is leading with dates and asking the witness to agree them rather than have the witness's testimony upon the dates which, in our submission, may be material to assess the reliability of recollection and, indeed, whether witnesses have heard by rumour or otherwise about what took place in Omarska on a particular date. I do make this objection on the basis that if dates are to be led to witnesses in this form, our submission is that the court is not assisted by assessing the reliability of the witness when it is not the witness's own testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the date of 18th June ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just the question. The objection is that it is leading. Do you remember if you were given biscuits, shared some biscuits on June 18th I think was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I hope I did not say June 18th, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 16th sorry. You said 18th I guess, Mr. Kay, did you, and I believed you or may be not. Anyway ----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If my friend insists on me doing it the long way I will do it the long way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: At this point it really does not make difference. I do not want to sustain the objection because we have indicated that our Rules are typically very liberal and that our concern is whether or not the evidence is probative. You are saying it is not probative because it is leading. I will sustain the objection because it does not make any difference. You can rephrase the question and ask him if he remembers sharing biscuits and, if so, on what date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will do that, your Honour. Mr. Mujcic, during the period of time when you were in Omarska camp do you recall an incident whereby you shared biscuits with other inmates in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it very well. Jasmin Hrnic mentioned a birthday, his child's birthday, although there were very many of us, and from somewhere somebody had brought a box of biscuits and he offered as much as he could. Some were given a half or a quarter of a biscuit, but those near him were all given something. We remembered it and I personally have it imprinted on my memory this piece of cake. I have never tasted anything as delicious as that biscuit, even though it was a tiny bit but it was a great deal for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the day you were eating this biscuit and there was reference to the fact that it was Hrnic's child's birthday, did the question of the date of that particular day arise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasko said, I remember it was 16th very well, he said that it was the birthday, but about the date, did he say "today"? "I could not see that child. I am offering you this for the sake of his birthday", but whether it was the same day, the birthday of Jasmin's child, but I remember he mentioned that those biscuits were intended for his child's birthday, that those were the biscuits for his child's birthday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall how many days after this particular day the event occurred where you said in your evidence you saw Dusko Tadic at Omarska camp in the large hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two days later after that biscuit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked a question about the position that you took in the column, and in your evidence-in-chief you had said that when you were walking by the old school: " ... I came closer to the well because I was at the end of the column." The use of the word "end" in that context when you were talking about your position, did you mean the end of the column in the sense of the final part of the column or the end of the column meaning the edge of the column closest to the well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The edge of the column closest to the well, not in front of the column or in the end of the column or somewhere in the middle, but to the side, at the edge of the column near the well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the witness now be shown Exhibit 223?
